verdict.rationale: CockroachDB documents running the same engine locally: Homebrew install, `cockroach demo` for a temporary in-memory cluster, and single-node clusters for app development. These cover offline development and testing. The 'keyless, no account' part is undercut by a community report that even free users need an annual license key, and nothing in the evidence documents a key-free path. missing for 10: evidence that local/CI use needs no license key or account, explicit CI-test guidance, independent hands-on corroboration of fully offline operation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run the same engine locally and keylessly — no account or cloud dependency — for offline development and CI tests

citations.quote: The `cockroach demo` starts a temporary, in-memory CockroachDB cluster of one or more nodes, with or without a preloaded dataset, and opens an interactive SQL shell to the cluster.
A single-node cluster is appropriate for quick SQL testing or app development.
